key-function corroboration: dBase_c declares exactly two virtuals of its own -- the destructor, defined INLINE in the header, and AfterInitResources. AfterInitResources is therefore the key function, and defining it as a real method emits _ZTV7dBase_c and pulls the destructor's two vague-linkage out-of-line copies into existence for free (5/5 MATCH, no forcing scaffold). That directly demonstrates that D1, D0 and AfterInitResources belong to ONE translation unit: compiling the key function makes the two destructor bodies exist and produces them in the ROM's own order. Production now checks the emitted vtable/RTTI against their canonical ROM homes through the manifest's deadstrip-data policy before discarding those copies from this text-only contribution.

destructor-variant order corroborates the source form independently of any of the above. mwcc emits an OUT-OF-LINE destructor definition as the fixed group D2,D0,D1 (notes/tu-reconstruction-pilot-report.md sec 3), and fBase_c -- destructor defined out of line -- has exactly that in the ROM (0x02043d48 D2, 0x02043d78 D0, 0x02043dbc D1). An INLINE destructor's vague-linkage copies come out D1-then-D0 with no D2. This class has D1 (0x02013e80) then D0 (0x02013ea4) and no D2 anywhere in the image -- matching the inline form include/dBase_c.h documents, and NOT matching a second out-of-line definition.
